verdict.rationale: Design is substantively complete and architecturally sound. All 11 routed decisions are addressed with concrete options + rationale + risk; F-003 BLOCKER (skills disable-model-invocation silent-drop) is mitigated by the runtime Read/Glob pattern (D-01) consistent with the cc-critique structural template (CP-001). The three-layer enforcement architecture (FR-3) is well-articulated and each layer's independence is shown explicitly. All four ACs the PRD routes to the CC layer are explicitly tied to design elements. No critical issues; minor consistency gaps remain.

issues.description: D-05 ownership inconsistency. Contents lists 'D-01, D-02, D-03, D-04, D-07, D-08, D-09, D-11, D-12, D-13, D-14' (11 decisions, excluding D-05/D-06/D-10). Layer Responsibility Scope says 'D-05 shared, D-06 owned, D-10 owned' by design-backend — implying D-05 is fully routed away. However: (a) synthesis §Per-layer Design Routing (line 336) explicitly routes D-05 as shared between design-cc + design-backend; (b) the cc-design body authors the D-05 per-state companion-field table inside §Templates and KB Edits → §issue-doctypes-spec.md §3 (lines 996-1005); (c) the §Sub-Agent Patterns body workflow cites D-05 directly (lines 273-282, line 310-311, 704); (d) cc-dependencies.json CONSUMES-SYNTH-01 includes D-05 in the consumed-decisions list NO — actually it does not (it lists 'D-01, D-02, D-03, D-04, D-07, D-08, D-09, D-11, D-12, D-13, D-14'). The body and the spec authoring contradict the routing declaration.

issues.location: Design body globally — no consolidated 'Verification Strategy' subsection
issues.description: Per the Gate 1 Verification Strategy quality check (per KB-review-disciplines): when a design replaces or modifies existing behavior, a concrete output comparison method must be defined; correctness definition must be specific and measurable; verification method must be sufficient for the change's risk; an early verification point must be identified. The cc-design DOES contain all this material — D-07 specifies the hook test strategy (shellcheck + golden-file fixtures + integration smoke), D-11 specifies the 1000-iteration p95 latency-measurement protocol with explicit thresholds (ratify ≤100ms; replace if ≤200ms; escalate if >200ms), D-13 specifies a migration dry-run with git-mv similarity-index verification — but these are scattered across §Mechanism Designs subsections. For a high-blast-radius change (the first hook in the project, the first PreToolUse interceptor that fires on every Task spawn), the verification posture should be locatable in one place.
issues.evidence: cc-design.md §D-07 (lines 675-696): hook test strategy. cc-design.md §D-11 (lines 736-754): latency measurement protocol. cc-design.md §D-13 (lines 768-797): migration dry-run. No labelled 'Verification Strategy' subsection. blueprint-template.md line 30 (Contents) and line 883 (body) require Verification Strategy in the Blueprint — design-composer can lift this material into the cross-cutting Blueprint subsection.
issues.suggestion: Add a short §Verification Strategy subsection (10-20 lines) at the end of the body (before §Open Items) that summarises: (a) correctness definition for each NFR (NFR-1 latency, NFR-2 fail-open, NFR-4 Write-gating, NFR-5 collision-handling); (b) verification method per primitive (shellcheck for hook; golden-file fixtures for fail-open branches; integration smoke for end-to-end; 1000-iteration p95 for latency; git-mv similarity-index dry-run for migration); (c) early verification point (recommend: hook script + shellcheck + golden-file fixtures land FIRST in the plan, since they catch the highest-blast-radius regression at lowest cost). This consolidation costs ~15-25 lines and gives design-composer a copy-source for the cross-cutting Verification Strategy.

issues.description: Per KB-general-coding-principles Dimension 10 (Sample is minimal — one block ≤ 40 lines): the agent-body workflow pseudocode block is ~145 lines and contains four sub-procedures (Create-mode, Update-mode, Evolution-transaction, Filename-collision branch). This is over the 40-line guideline. Score would be ~70 on Dimension 10. The block is documentation-pseudocode rather than runtime code, but it is presented as a single fenced block intended to be copy-paste into the agent file.
issues.evidence: cc-design.md lines 234-380 (~145 lines in one fenced block under '## Procedure').
issues.suggestion: Split into 4 named fenced blocks with prose between: (1) 'At task start' (~10 lines), (2) 'Phase 1: Dispatch by mode → Create-mode' (~40 lines), (3) 'Update-mode' (~15 lines), (4) 'Evolution-transaction' (~20 lines), (5) 'Filename-collision branch' (~15 lines), plus 'Observability' and 'Hard constraints' as separate blocks. This improves readability for plan-author at Stage 8 (Plan Authoring) when porting these blocks into the actual agent file.

issues.description: The example PreToolUse stdin event JSON is documented as 'per KB-cc-platform/references/extensions.md hook contract; assumption-verification flagged in §Open Items'. The Open Item U-1 (lines 1111) correctly identifies this as unverified against live Claude Code platform docs and routes verification to plan-author. However, the design proceeds to use this assumption in D-02 (script structure that depends on `.tool_input.subagent_type`), D-03 (hook stdout schema), and D-11 (latency-measurement protocol). If the field is named differently in the live platform (e.g., `subAgentType`, `agent_type`, nested under a different key), the hook script's jq path AND the test-fixture authoring would need to change. This is correctly flagged but no fallback strategy is documented.
issues.evidence: cc-design.md lines 569-580 (example stdin); lines 1111 (U-1 verification deferred to plan-author).
issues.suggestion: Add a brief 'If verification at plan stage reveals the field is named differently' note to U-1, stating: (a) the jq path becomes `.tool_input.<actual-field-name>` and only that one line of the hook script changes; (b) the golden-file fixtures (D-07 layer B) must be updated; (c) the architecture (three-layer enforcement, fail-open posture, latency target) is unaffected. Cost: 3 lines, prevents loop-back at plan stage.

issues.description: The section enumerates 17 AC mappings. issues.suggestion: Either (a) expand §Acceptance Criteria Contribution to cover every PRD AC that this CC layer is responsible for testing (including the FR-8 migration ACs that this design owns), OR (b) add a one-line note at the start of §Acceptance Criteria Contribution: 'This section lists the load-bearing ACs whose testability depends on a specific design element; other CC-routed ACs are testable from the surface form of the artifacts (per-issue folder model, frontmatter shape, etc.) without specific design-element coupling.' Option (b) is lower-cost. Plan-author / test-acceptance-author will enumerate the full AC list.

issues.location: Multiple — D-04 examples paths, D-13 migration map, examples in §References
issues.description: Per the AC-FR-1-c and AC-FR-1-e references, the design correctly distinguishes pre-migration vs post-migration paths. However, D-04's example pairing table (lines 666-672) shows POST-migration paths, while D-13's migration map (lines 774-780) shows the pre→post mapping. A reader scanning quickly could miss that the D-04 example paths only become valid AFTER the D-13 migration completes. D-04 does note this in the 'Authoring constraint per D-13' subtle (line 673), but a cross-link from D-04 → D-13 (and vice-versa) would prevent confusion when these sections are read independently.
issues.evidence: cc-design.md lines 666-672 (D-04 table uses post-migration paths); cc-design.md lines 774-780 (D-13 migration map).
issues.suggestion: Add a one-line cross-reference at the head of D-04: 'POST-migration paths used below — see §D-13 for the migration map and §D-13 for the authoring-sequence constraint that examples.md is written in the same atomic commit as the migration.' Cost: 1 line.

issues.description: AC-NFR-9-a is paraphrased: 'While the user is in any Claude Code session, the system shall accept /capture-issue <hint> without context-switch.' The PRD verbatim phrasing (prd-v2.md line 454) is: 'without requiring the user to context-switch, run an external tool, or open a different window.' The design's paraphrase drops two of the three concrete failure modes (external tool, different window). For a Gate-0-traceable AC, verbatim or near-verbatim transcription is preferred.
issues.evidence: prd-v2.md line 454: full AC-NFR-9-a text. cc-design.md line 1077: paraphrased.
issues.suggestion: Restore the full AC text: 'While the user is in any Claude Code session, the system shall accept /capture-issue <hint> without requiring the user to context-switch, run an external tool, or open a different window. [Skill activation pattern.]' Cost: half a line.

issues.location: Fact Disposition Table (absent — per-layer Design subsection)
issues.description: Per Gate 1's fact-disposition-completeness check (when codebase_analysis is provided): every entry in focusAreas requires a corresponding row in a Fact Disposition Table. The codebase-analysis.json has 16 findings (F-001..F-016) — equivalent to focusAreas. The cc-design references these findings extensively throughout (F-001..F-007 in §Project Precedents Established; F-010/F-013/F-014/F-015 in §D-14; F-016 in §Open Items U-1) but does not consolidate the dispositions into a single table. NOTE: per the v4.3.0 blueprint template, the Fact Disposition Table is a CROSS-CUTTING section authored by design-composer at Stage 7, not per-layer. So this is not a per-layer Gate 0 failure. It IS material that design-composer needs as input.
issues.evidence: codebase-analysis.json findings array (F-001..F-016, 16 entries); cc-design.md references findings throughout but does not table them.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief 'CC-layer Fact Dispositions' subsection (16 rows max) just before §References. Each row: fact_id | one-line disposition (preserve/transform/remove/out-of-scope) | rationale (one phrase). This isn't a Gate 0 requirement at the per-layer level, but it would directly feed design-composer's Stage 7 Fact Disposition Table without re-derivation. Cost: ~20 lines.

issues.description: Per KB-general-coding-principles Dimension 6 (No hidden control flow): the hook script uses `set -u` (no -e per inline rationale 'we want to control all exit paths explicitly'). This is sound for a fail-open hook. Per Dimension 3 (Error contract visible): the script's error paths are visible (jq parse failure detected at line 408-412, malformed stdin detected at line 409). Per Dimension 7 (Idempotency stated): the hook is idempotent (no side effects beyond stderr + stdout) but this isn't explicit in the script's prose. Per Dimension 8 (Concurrency posture stated): multiple Task tools can spawn in parallel; each hook invocation is independent (no shared state). The design body does not explicitly call out either dimension.
issues.suggestion: Add a one-line comment in the hook script: '# Idempotent: no side effects beyond stderr/stdout; no shared state; concurrent Task spawns each get an independent invocation.' Cost: 1 line.

recommendations: Address the three conditions before promoting status: draft → status: accepted on the per-layer Design subsection.

Reconcile D-05 ownership in both cc-design.md AND cc-dependencies.json (CONSUMES-SYNTH-01 ids list) so reviewers and design-backend can locate the canonical per-state companion-field table without confusion.

Consider adding a labelled 'Verification Strategy' subsection (I-DR-003) — this work product becomes design-composer's direct input for the cross-cutting Blueprint Verification Strategy, reducing Stage 7 composition cost.
Consider authoring the CC-layer Fact Disposition rows (I-DR-009) for the same reason — direct input to design-composer's cross-cutting Fact Disposition Table.

All five Q-CC-N (Q-CC-1..5) are well-formed for composer arbitration. Q-CC-1 (audit-trail ADR consolidation) is the highest-value question — design-composer's resolution of this drives the 7-ADR slate cardinality from synthesis U-10.

Strong rationale verification: F-003 BLOCKER mitigation (D-01) is correctly architected — runtime Read/Glob substitutes for the broken skills: preload, with cc-critique (CP-001) as the in-project structural precedent. The audit trail (SETTINGS-NOTES + ADR + non-pollution-contract.md cross-references) is well-designed.

The three-layer enforcement architecture (§Three-Layer Enforcement Architecture, lines 1025-1041) is the strongest section of the design — each layer's independence is shown with a bypass-cost analysis. This is publication-quality and should be lifted verbatim into the Stage 7 ADR for three-layer enforcement (U-10 item 4).
